newsitem.title: KENYA: Human tide of refugees on the move in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Human tide of refugees on the move in Zaire.

text.p: A stream of about 200,000 Rwandan refugees fled westwards on Sunday after one of eastern Zaire's biggest camps was reported to have been shelled from Rwanda and several refugees were killed, a senior aid worker said.
"There is a stream of people about 25 km (15 miles) long...I saw pregnant women, handicapped people, little children," U.N. official Panos Moumtzis said by telephone from the Zairean town of Goma.

Moumtzis, a spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), told Reuters refugees said sustained artillery attacks on the Kibumba camp on the night of Friday to Saturday had come from the direction of Rwanda.

"We saw four dead bodies in Kibumba, but refugees told us there were a lot more dead...We were told there were at least 100 wounded," said Moumtzis, who visited the now abandoned camp 25 km (15 miles) north of Goma on Sunday morning.
"One of the mortars hit Kibumba hospital. They told us there were a lot of patients inside and it was absolute chaos," he said.

More than one million Rwandan Hutu refugees have lived in a string of camps in eastern Zaire since 1994. They fled Rwanda fearing reprisals for the 1994 genocide in which Hutus killed up to one million Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
About half a million of these refugees are on the move after a series of attacks by Tutsi rebels fighting Zairean troops in eastern Zaire.
The armies of both Rwanda and Burundi, Zaire's small neighbours to the east, are dominated by the Tutsi minorities and diplomats fear they are being drawn into the conflict.

A central objective for both countries is the closure of the Hutu refugee camps located right on their borders and used as bases for Hutu rebel infiltrators. This objective is being achieved by the past fortnight's fighting.
Zaire says Rwanda is sending troops to support Tutsi rebels, a charge Rwanda denies.

Moumtzis said the refugees who had fled Kibumba were being directed to a camp at Mugunga 13 km (eight miles) west of Goma. "About 5,000 refugees an hour are entering Mugunga," he said, adding that by Monday evening all of the refugees should have arrived there.
He said U.N. staff with loudspeakers were telling refugees not to enter Goma city.
There were reports several thousand refugees had been forced by the fighting to cross into Rwanda, the homeland where they fear persecution or punishment for genocide crimes.
Paul Stromberg, UNHCR spokesman in the Rwanda capital Kigali, said between 5,000 and 10,000 Rwandan refugees fled into Rwanda from eastern Zaire on Sunday morning at the border post of Mutura.
